newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen stuck in range below 123.00.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen stuck in range below 123.00.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be range-bound below 123.00 on Friday, as market players adopt a cautious stance ahead of release of key U.S. jobs data, traders said.

"I think activity will be limited to position adjustment ahead of the weekend... The U.S. jobs data also looms ahead, which will make it hard to move sharply in either direction," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Recent firmness in the cash JGB market, due to investor buying and dealer buying of the 190th JGB, may provide some support, traders said.

"Some buying of cash bonds by investors was detected recently. This may lead to a tight supply/demand balance in the cash bond market, and would provide support to JGBs," a trader for a major brokerage house said.
Dealers have been buying the 190th JGB recently, on speculation that it will become the new cash JGB benchmark in the near future, the first trader said.

The November and October 190th JGBs, both of which were issued with the same terms in 1996, are due to be combined on Friday, 10 business days before the first interest payments on both issues are due.
The U.S. May nonfarm payrolls report is due at 1230 GMT on Friday.
Economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, that nonfarm payrolls would rise by 219,000 given the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics' seasonal revisions announced last Friday.
That was a small decline from the original consensus on a rise of 221,000.
